name: tripo
description: Generate 3D models with Tripo from Hermes: text, image or multiview to 3D, helper images, texturing, rigging and animation, retopology, segmentation and format conversion. Game Studio turns a model into a character you control, played in the Desktop card, as a three.js web prototype or in Godot, Unity or Unreal. Runs Tripo's official tripo-cli MCP server locally (pinned tripo-cli@0.9.0 over npx stdio, international accounts, your Tripo API key) with the tripo-3d and tripo-game-asset workflow skills. Credit-spending calls ask for approval first. In Hermes Desktop: inline 3D cards with Next and Download menus and a Play mode, a Tripo 3D gallery and a credit chip.

api_key.label: Tripo API key
api_key.description: Create one at developers.tripo3d.ai/en/keys (international Tripo account). Saving it restarts the Tripo tools with the new key.

show_credits.label: Credit balance in the status bar
show_credits.description: Desktop: show remaining Tripo credits in the status bar.

inline_viewer.label: Inline 3D cards in chat
inline_viewer.description: Desktop: render ::tripo-model replies as interactive 3D cards. Off shows them as text.

auto_rotate.label: Auto-rotate in the gallery
auto_rotate.description: Desktop: slowly spin the model in the gallery viewer.

gallery_limit.label: Recent generations shown
gallery_limit.description: How many recent Tripo generations the Desktop list shows (1-60).

blender_handoff.label: Blender optimized copy
blender_handoff.description: When Blender is installed, offer an optimized copy for game testing after a download (packed textures, optional triangle budget, new .blend + GLB/FBX). Runs locally, no Tripo credits. Ask offers it once.

default_model.label: Default 3D model
default_model.description: How the Tripo skill picks the 3D generation model when you do not name one. Ask offers v3.1, P2 and P1 with their credits; v3.1 (general use, about 20-30 credits textured) or P2 (games and real-time, about 110) is used without asking. The plan still shows the price for your yes.

blender_path.label: Blender executable
blender_path.description: Full path to Blender 4.2 or newer. Empty finds it on PATH or in the usual install folders.
